answer.summary: For a linear regression model with an intercept and 3 predictors testing whether population R² differs from zero at α = 0.05 with anticipated multiple correlation ρ = 0.30 and target power of 90%, the minimum integer total sample size is 148 participants. This achieves 90.16% power using the noncentral F test with 3 numerator and 144 denominator degrees of freedom, noncentrality parameter λ = 14.64, and critical F-value 2.667. The preceding admissible design at N = 147 achieves 89.94% power, confirming that N = 148 is the minimum integer sample size meeting the 90% power criterion.

Critical F-value obtained from central F(3, n-4) distribution at significance level α = 0.05. Power computed as P(F(3, n-4, λ) > F_crit) from noncentral F distribution. Minimum integer sample size identified by grid search: N = 148 satisfies power ≥ 0.90; N = 147 does not.
assumptions: Fixed linear regression model with intercept and k = 3 predictors
Test statistic: F = [R²/k]/[(1-R²)/(n-k-1)] follows noncentral F(k, n-k-1, λ) under H₁
Errors normally distributed with constant variance
limitations: Assumes correctly specified model (correct functional form, no omitted confounders)
Effect size ρ = 0.30 must be accurately anticipated; power is sensitive to underestimation
No inflation for attrition or missing data; actual enrollment should account for dropout if anticipated
Assumes no variable selection post-hoc; conducted model selection alters actual Type I error
Does not account for potential multicollinearity among predictors, which reduces effective power

# Design parameters
alpha <- 0.05
target_power <- 0.90
rho <- 0.30  # anticipated multiple correlation
k <- 3       # number of predictors
p <- k + 1   # degrees of freedom numerator (k predictors)

# For two-sided test, use alpha/2 for each tail in F test
# The F test is inherently one-sided (testing against larger values)
alpha_f <- alpha  # For F-test, we compare to critical value at alpha level

# Noncentrality parameter: lambda = n * rho^2 / (1 - rho^2)
# Effect size: f^2 = rho^2 / (1 - rho^2)
f_squared <- rho^2 / (1 - rho^2)

# Grid search for minimum sample size
sample_sizes <- seq(10, 200, by = 1)
powers <- numeric(length(sample_sizes))

for (i in seq_along(sample_sizes)) {
  n <- sample_sizes[i]
  df1 <- k           # numerator df
  df2 <- n - k - 1   # denominator df
  
  # Noncentrality parameter
  lambda <- n * f_squared
  
  # Critical F value (one-sided test at alpha level)
  f_crit <- qf(1 - alpha_f, df1, df2)
  
  # Power from noncentral F distribution
  power <- 1 - pf(f_crit, df1, df2, lambda)
  powers[i] <- power
}

# Find minimum sample size achieving target power
min_idx <- which(powers >= target_power)[1]
min_sample_size <- sample_sizes[min_idx]
achieved_power <- powers[min_idx]

# Also report the sample size just below minimum for comparison
if (min_idx > 1) {
  prev_sample_size <- sample_sizes[min_idx - 1]
  prev_power <- powers[min_idx - 1]
} else {
  prev_sample_size <- NA
  prev_power <- NA
}

# Display results
cat("=== Linear Regression R² Test Sample Size Calculation ===\n")
cat("Null hypothesis: H₀: ρ² = 0\n")
cat("Alternative hypothesis: H₁: ρ² ≠ 0 (two-sided)\n")
cat("Test: Noncentral F test\n\n")
cat("Design parameters:\n")
cat("  Significance level (α):", alpha, "\n")
cat("  Target power:", target_power, "\n")
cat("  Anticipated multiple correlation (ρ):", rho, "\n")
cat("  Number of predictors (k):", k, "\n")
cat("  Numerator df:", k, "\n")
cat("  Effect size (f² = ρ²/(1-ρ²)):", round(f_squared, 6), "\n\n")

cat("Sample size search:\n")
cat("  Minimum sample size achieving 90% power: N =", min_sample_size, "\n")
cat("  Achieved power at N =", min_sample_size, ":", round(achieved_power, 4), "\n")

if (!is.na(prev_sample_size)) {
  cat("  Power at N =", prev_sample_size, "(preceding design):", round(prev_power, 4), "\n")
}

# Detailed calculation for minimum sample size
n_min <- min_sample_size
df1_min <- k
df2_min <- n_min - k - 1
lambda_min <- n_min * f_squared
f_crit_min <- qf(1 - alpha_f, df1_min, df2_min)
power_min <- 1 - pf(f_crit_min, df1_min, df2_min, lambda_min)

cat("\nDetailed calculation for N =", n_min, ":\n")
cat("  Denominator df: n - k - 1 =", n_min, "-", k, "- 1 =", df2_min, "\n")
cat("  Noncentrality parameter (λ): n × f² =", n_min, "×", round(f_squared, 6), "=", round(lambda_min, 4), "\n")

  critical_f_value = round(f_crit_min, 4)
)

# Evidence e1; success=true

# Design parameters
alpha <- 0.05
target_power <- 0.90
rho <- 0.30  # anticipated multiple correlation
k <- 3       # number of predictors
p <- k + 1   # degrees of freedom numerator (k predictors)

# For two-sided test, use alpha/2 for each tail in F test
# The F test is inherently one-sided (testing against larger values)
alpha_f <- alpha  # For F-test, we compare to critical value at alpha level

# Noncentrality parameter: lambda = n * rho^2 / (1 - rho^2)
# Effect size: f^2 = rho^2 / (1 - rho^2)
f_squared <- rho^2 / (1 - rho^2)

# Grid search for minimum sample size
sample_sizes <- seq(10, 200, by = 1)
powers <- numeric(length(sample_sizes))

for (i in seq_along(sample_sizes)) {
  n <- sample_sizes[i]
  df1 <- k           # numerator df
  df2 <- n - k - 1   # denominator df
  
  # Noncentrality parameter
  lambda <- n * f_squared
  
  # Critical F value (one-sided test at alpha level)
  f_crit <- qf(1 - alpha_f, df1, df2)
  
  # Power from noncentral F distribution
  power <- 1 - pf(f_crit, df1, df2, lambda)
  powers[i] <- power
}

# Find minimum sample size achieving target power
min_idx <- which(powers >= target_power)[1]
min_sample_size <- sample_sizes[min_idx]
achieved_power <- powers[min_idx]

# Also report the sample size just below minimum for comparison
if (min_idx > 1) {
  prev_sample_size <- sample_sizes[min_idx - 1]
  prev_power <- powers[min_idx - 1]
} else {
  prev_sample_size <- NA
  prev_power <- NA
}

# Display results
cat("=== Linear Regression R² Test Sample Size Calculation ===\n")
cat("Null hypothesis: H₀: ρ² = 0\n")
cat("Alternative hypothesis: H₁: ρ² ≠ 0 (two-sided)\n")
cat("Test: Noncentral F test\n\n")
cat("Design parameters:\n")
cat("  Significance level (α):", alpha, "\n")
cat("  Target power:", target_power, "\n")
cat("  Anticipated multiple correlation (ρ):", rho, "\n")
cat("  Number of predictors (k):", k, "\n")
cat("  Numerator df:", k, "\n")
cat("  Effect size (f² = ρ²/(1-ρ²)):", round(f_squared, 6), "\n\n")

cat("Sample size search:\n")
cat("  Minimum sample size achieving 90% power: N =", min_sample_size, "\n")
cat("  Achieved power at N =", min_sample_size, ":", round(achieved_power, 4), "\n")

if (!is.na(prev_sample_size)) {
  cat("  Power at N =", prev_sample_size, "(preceding design):", round(prev_power, 4), "\n")
}

# Detailed calculation for minimum sample size
n_min <- min_sample_size
df1_min <- k
df2_min <- n_min - k - 1
lambda_min <- n_min * f_squared
f_crit_min <- qf(1 - alpha_f, df1_min, df2_min)
power_min <- 1 - pf(f_crit_min, df1_min, df2_min, lambda_min)

cat("\nDetailed calculation for N =", n_min, ":\n")
cat("  Denominator df: n - k - 1 =", n_min, "-", k, "- 1 =", df2_min, "\n")
cat("  Noncentrality parameter (λ): n × f² =", n_min, "×", round(f_squared, 6), "=", round(lambda_min, 4), "\n")
cat("  Critical F value (F₃,₍ₙ₋₄₎; 1-α):", round(f_crit_min, 4), "\n")
cat("  Power = P(F(3,", df2_min, ", λ=", round(lambda_min, 4), ") > ", round(f_crit_min, 4), ") =", round(power_min, 4), "\n")

# Return structured result
result <- list(
  sample_size = min_sample_size,
  achieved_power = round(achieved_power, 4),
  preceding_sample_size = ifelse(is.na(prev_sample_size), NA, prev_sample_size),
  preceding_power = ifelse(is.na(prev_power), NA, round(prev_power, 4)),
  target_power = target_power,
  alpha = alpha,
  noncentrality_parameter = round(lambda_min, 4),
  critical_f_value = round(f_crit_min, 4)
)

library(jsonlite)
cat("\n\nStructured output:\n")
print(toJSON(result, auto_unbox = TRUE, digits = 15))
